note: Phase 0 baseline — classic MCTS, single-process, torch.set_num_threads(1), CPU. Timings recorded via fast_mcts/bench.py monkey-patch instrumentation. Compare future fast backend against these.

takeaways.real_net_bottleneck: network.inference dominates at 70%+ wall at sims=100 (10k+ calls, batch=1, ~1.23 ms/call). Leaf batching (Phase 1) is the largest available lever.
takeaways.fake_net_bottleneck: env.step (40%+) + python MCTS overhead (select/legal/features/clone ~35%). Relevant for when GPU NN becomes cheap — then Phase 3 vec_env and Phase 4 flat-tree matter.
takeaways.phase1_theoretical_max: Batching N leaves into one fwd pass collapses 70.5% -> ~70.5%/N at ideal GPU scaling. With N=32 and real GPU, expect ~10-15x end-to-end self-play throughput.

phase1_results.note: fast backend: leaf-gather + virtual loss (lc0-style), AlphaDev semantics preserved at vl=0/batch=1. Measured on CPU (same hardware as baseline).
phase1_results.config: map=2, sims=100, 3 games, real net, CPU, torch.set_num_threads(1)

fast_parity_mode.note: byte-identical to classic, same wall — correctness + regression guard

phase1_results.remaining_bottleneck: env.step (31%) + env.legal_actions (13%) dominate at batch=32. These are the Phase 3 (vec_env) targets.
phase1_results.expected_gpu_gain: On GPU the per-call ~1.3 ms drops by 5-10x due to kernel-launch amortization → fast_batch32 should be ~15-25x vs classic on GPU.
